entry_point: Library API: message composition (addAttachmentPart, addAttachmentPartFromFile, addInlineImage, renameAttachment, setTextPart/setHtmlPart, setAsMultipartSigned, setSignature) and message reading (MailMimeParser::parse with getSubject, getFilename, getHeaderParameter)

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned commit: a value supplied while composing a message (attachment name, inline-image name or content id, renamed name, body charset, signing parameters) with a CRLF and a header-like line makes the library write that line as a real header into the serialised message; a value decoded while reading a message (RFC 2231 parameter, split continuation, RFC 2047 encoded-word, quoted-pair continuation) comes back through the public getters with the line break intact, and the signing path writes a decoded parameter into a new raw header. All driven through MailMimeParser::parse and the public IMessage/IMimePart/IUUEncodedPart API; no network.

src/Header/Part/MimeToken.php:46 RFC 2047 decoding: the existing CR/LF removal runs before decodeMime, so decoded line breaks survive - published-fix far site (header/part decoder, a different module from the message helper)
src/Header/Part/ParameterPart.php:65-71 RFC 2231 decodePartValue (also reached by SplitParameterPart::getValueFromParts) - published-fix far site

src/Message/Helper/MultipartHelper.php:277 and :390 charset value interpolated raw into Content-Type, on the create-new-part and existing-part paths

routes: Pattern B routes confirmed behaviourally at the pinned commit (see build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv): quoted-pair continuations in quoted and unquoted parameter values (still present in current upstream); caller-supplied signing parameters; body charset on both content-part paths; a non-MIME attachment name written to the begin line. The last three were later fixed upstream with a shared control-character stripper, which confirms them as real routes of the same family.
The decoded-value re-emission route (a decoded parameter copied into a new raw header by the signing path) is confirmed through the public API and is part of the same decoded-value lever.
injected_siblings: src/Message.php addInlineImage -> MultipartHelper::createAndAddPartForInlineImage: a neighbouring inline-image feature with its own name handling and a Content-ID header; reachable from the same public message API.
src/Message.php renameAttachment -> MultipartHelper::setAttachmentFilename: an attachment-naming feature with its own name handling; reachable from the same public message API.

The full project suite (609 tests) also passes on the reference fix at build time; the pinned checkout's own suite passes on the pinned tree.

patch_checks.why: keeps the strip before the RFC 2047 decode and the RFC 2231 decode unprotected, and keeps the decoded protocol re-emitted
leaves literal quoted-pair continuations carrying a line break
leaves the body charset raw on both content-part paths
leaves a non-MIME attachment name raw in the begin line
leaves the injected inline-image name and content id raw
leaves the injected rename path raw
strips line breaks inside the raw-header setter, destroying the library's own folded header layout
refuses every composition operation, so ordinary use stops working

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: for a library call an exception is an accepted refusal and the security tests accept it; the functional suite is the positive control that a whole-operation refusal cannot pass.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no authorisation decision or neighbouring resource; the protected outcome is the text of the message the library writes.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the library looks up no authority, secret or role on these paths.

traps.lever: attachment name supplied by the application
traps.shape: a caller-supplied attachment name containing CR/LF followed by a header-like line

traps.lever: values decoded from a message: the existing CR/LF removal runs before the RFC 2047 decode, and the RFC 2231 decode path removes nothing; split continuations inherit it; a decoded parameter is re-emitted into a new header when signing
traps.shape: encoded-word whose decoded text contains CR/LF; percent-encoded parameter value (%0D%0A) with and without a charset; split continuations; decoded protocol parameter copied into a header
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the parser only reads messages, and a decoded value is supposed to return the true decoded text; the existing CR/LF removal in the token layer looks like the defence
traps.realistic_because: published fix sites in a lower-level module the report does not mention

traps.lever: quoted-pair continuations are passed as literal tokens and skip the token-level CR/LF removal, in quoted and unquoted parameter values; the quoted-literal class documentation claims CR/LF are stripped, but the code does not strip them
traps.shape: backslash followed by CRLF inside a quoted filename parameter, and the same continuation in an unquoted parameter value
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a quoted-pair line continuation is just folding, and both the token layer's removal and the quoted-literal class documentation claim the value is already stripped
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (still present in current upstream)

traps.lever: signing parameters supplied by the application are interpolated raw into the composed Content-Type
traps.shape: CR/LF and a header-like line in the algorithm or protocol value given when signing a message
traps.reason_to_dismiss: signing is a separate feature whose algorithm and protocol are developer-chosen constants, not attachment data
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; fixed by a later upstream commit, not by the published advisory fix

traps.lever: the charset supplied with the body is interpolated raw into the composed Content-Type, on both the create-new-part and the existing-part paths
traps.shape: CR/LF and a header-like line in the charset value, on a message without a body part and on one that already has one
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the charset is developer configuration rather than user data, and the two paths are neighbouring features
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; fixed by a later upstream commit, not by the published advisory fix

traps.pattern: B (uncovered route, protection never existed there)
traps.lever: a non-MIME attachment's name is stored raw and written into the uuencoded begin line
traps.shape: CR/LF and a header-like line in the name set on a non-MIME message's attachment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the uuencode path is legacy and the begin line is not an email header; the writer lives in a separate package
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; fixed by a later upstream commit, not by the published advisory fix

traps.lever: an inline-image API added next to the attachment API has its own name handling and writes a Content-ID header
traps.shape: CR/LF and a header-like line in the inline image's name, and in its content id
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an inline image is a neighbouring feature, not the attachment path the report names, and the same code shape looks handled elsewhere
traps.realistic_because: injected: a plausible maintainer addition alongside the existing attachment API, our-copy only

traps.lever: an attachment-renaming API added next to the attachment API rebuilds the disposition header from its own unsanitised name
traps.shape: CR/LF and a header-like line in the new name given for an existing attachment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the caller is setting a name directly on an existing part, which reads as trusted configuration rather than creation-time user data
traps.realistic_because: injected: a plausible maintainer addition alongside the existing attachment API, our-copy only
